<h2>The Purpose of Messengers: A Call to Awaken from Heedlessness</h2><p class="mainText">Impurity arises from filth (<span class="inlineArabic">نجاست</span>). The transition from a state of impurity to one of purity is called <span class="inlineArabic">طهارة</span> (purification). Since a human being is a composition of both the body and the soul (<span class="inlineArabic">نفس</span>), purifying the soul is as essential as purifying the body. Physical purity is achieved through the performance of outward religious acts, whereas the purification of the soul is attained by acquiring the inner knowledge (<span class="inlineArabic">معرفت</span>) of the spiritual realities (<span class="inlineArabic">ممثولات</span>) behind these external rites.</p><p class="mainText">Bodily purification is performed with water, while the purification of the soul is accomplished through knowledge. The Noble Prophet (PBUH) states, &ldquo;There is no <span class="inlineArabic">صلاة</span> (prayer) without <span class="inlineArabic">طهارة</span> (purity).&rdquo;</p><p class="mainText"><span class="inlineArabic">الوضوء</span> (Ablution) is a method for the evacuation of gross matter (<span class="inlineArabic">فضلات ھابطۃ</span>) from the body.</p><p class="mainText"><span class="inlineArabic">الوضوء</span> signifies the recognition of the Huduud (ranks/limits) of the Imam (<span class="inlineArabic">امام علیہ السلام</span>), and the <span class="inlineArabic">صلاة</span> (prayer) is evidence of establishing oneself within the Da&lsquo;wah (spiritual mission) of the Imam (<span class="inlineArabic">امام علیہ السلام</span>) through these Huduud. Since it is impossible to be established in the Imam&rsquo;s Da&lsquo;wah without recognizing the Huduud and making them one&#39;s means, <span class="inlineArabic">صلاة</span> is not valid without <span class="inlineArabic">وضوء</span>.</p><p class="mainText">Indeed, purity is half of <span class="inlineArabic">ایمان</span> (Faith). The Messenger of Allah (PBUH) stated that whoever perfects their <span class="inlineArabic">طهارة</span> and then leaves their house for the mosque to pray is considered to be in the state of <span class="inlineArabic">صلاة</span> until their <span class="inlineArabic">وضوء</span> is broken. This means that with <span class="inlineArabic">وضوء</span>, the descent of divine spiritual confirmations (<span class="inlineArabic">تائیدات</span>) and illuminations (<span class="inlineArabic">اشراقات</span>) from the Imam (<span class="inlineArabic">امام علیہ السلام</span>) begins upon the believer.</p><p class="mainText">The Messenger of Allah (PBUH) stated that the foundation of <span class="inlineArabic">صلاة</span> is built upon four things. Whoever fails to complete them, their prayer is a deception! These four things are:</p><table><thead><tr><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">1</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">2</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">3</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">4</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Perfect <span class="inlineArabic">وضوء</span></td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;"><span class="inlineArabic">رکوع</span> (Bowing)</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;"><span class="inlineArabic">سجود</span> (Prostration)</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;"><span class="inlineArabic">خشوع</span> (Humility)</td></tr></tbody></table><p class="mainText">Among these four essentials, perfect <span class="inlineArabic">وضوء</span> is the very first. The perfection of <span class="inlineArabic">وضوء</span> is achieved by repeating each step three times. Water represents the good deeds (<span class="inlineArabic">حسنات</span>) of the believers, which Allah has divided into three parts. Due to these three divisions, each part of <span class="inlineArabic">وضوء</span> is repeated three times. For the same reason, one is instructed to drink water in three gulps. Likewise, knowledge is also divided into the three parts of <span class="inlineArabic">شریعت</span> (Law), <span class="inlineArabic">تأویل</span> (Esoteric Interpretation), and <span class="inlineArabic">حقائق</span> (Ultimate Realities). Washing or wiping each limb three times signifies the recognition of the three Huduud of the Da&lsquo;wah (Spiritual Mission): <span class="inlineArabic">الناطق</span> (The Speaker-Prophet), <span class="inlineArabic">الاساس</span> (The Foundation), and <span class="inlineArabic">الإمام</span> (The Imam).</p><h2 class="mainText">(Purity)&nbsp;</h2><p class="mainText">When a believer performs <span class="inlineArabic">وضوء</span> once, they come into the sight of the Dai al-Waqt (Summoner of the Age), meaning the Dai perceives their pure intention (<span class="inlineArabic">حسن نیت</span>). When they repeat the action a second time, Allah grants them double the reward, and they enter the <em>Wilaayah</em> (Authority) of the Imam al-Zamaan (Imam of the Time), through which they attain spiritual purity (<span class="inlineArabic">باطنی طہارت</span>). When they perform the act a third time, the Prophet (<span class="inlineArabic">الپیغمبر علیہ السلام</span> - The Speaker) declares, &ldquo;This is my <span class="inlineArabic">وضوء</span> and the <span class="inlineArabic">وضوء</span> of the Prophets over whom I am the Master!&rdquo; This means they have reached the rank of &#39;Perfection&#39; (<span class="inlineArabic">کمال</span>).</p><p class="mainText">Purifying each limb three times indicates that when the believer completes their obligatory duties three times&mdash;that is, when they achieve the perfect knowledge of the Dai al-Waqt, the Imam al-Zamaan, and the Naatiq ash-Shari&lsquo;ah (The Speaker of the Law)&mdash;their rank is elevated, and they become included among the Huduud ad-Din (Ranks of Religion). In essence, <span class="inlineArabic">وضوء</span> is a means of being included among the Huduud of the Imam (<span class="inlineArabic">امام علیہ السلام</span>).</p><table><thead><tr><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">First Time</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Second Time</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Third Time</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Sight of the Dai</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;"><em>Wilaayah</em> of the Imam</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;"><span class="inlineArabic">وضوء</span> of the Naatiq</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Outer Purity</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Inner Purity</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Perfection</td></tr></tbody></table><p class="mainText"><span class="inlineArabic">الطهارة</span> relates to the purification of seven limbs, four of which are obligatory (<span class="inlineArabic">فرض</span>) and three are recommendable (<span class="inlineArabic">سنت</span>). Every act of purification signifies a specific rank in the spiritual and physical Da&lsquo;wah.</p><table><thead><tr><th colspan="4" style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Obligatory (<span class="inlineArabic">فرض</span>)</th><th colspan="3" style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Recommendable (<span class="inlineArabic">سنت</span>)</th></tr><tr><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">1</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">2</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">3</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">4</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">5</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">6</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">7</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Washing the Face</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Washing Both Hands (to the Elbows)</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Wiping the Head</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Wiping Both Feet (to the Ankles)</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Washing the Hands (to the Wrist)</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Rinsing the Mouth</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Rinsing the Nose</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;"><span class="inlineArabic">ناطق</span> (Speaker)</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;"><span class="inlineArabic">اساس</span> (Foundation)</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;"><span class="inlineArabic">عقل کل</span> (Universal Intellect)</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;"><span class="inlineArabic">نفس کل</span> (Universal Soul)</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;"><span class="inlineArabic">داعی</span> (Summoner)</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;"><span class="inlineArabic">حجت</span> (Proof)</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;"><span class="inlineArabic">امام</span> (Imam)</td></tr></tbody></table><h2 class="mainText">(Ablution)</h2><p class="mainText">In addition to these seven steps of <span class="inlineArabic">طهارة</span>, water touches the two hands, the face, the two arms, and the two feet, which are also a total of seven limbs. These seven Huduud (ranks) of <span class="inlineArabic">طهارة</span> signify the seven Speakers (<span class="inlineArabic">نطقا</span>), seven Imams (<span class="inlineArabic">آئمہ</span>), and seven Foundations (<span class="inlineArabic">اساس</span>) in different cycles. Furthermore, they refer to the seven spiritual ranks from the believer to the Imam:</p><table><thead><tr><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">1</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">2</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">3</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">4</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">5</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">6</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">7</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Hujjat</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Baab</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Mukallib</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">1</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">2</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">3</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">4</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">5</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">6</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">7</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">8</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">9</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">10</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">11</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">12</td></tr></tbody><tbody><tr><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Evacuation</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Cleansing after Evacuation</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Washing Both Hands</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Rinsing Mouth and Using Miswaak</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Intention (<span class="inlineArabic">نیت</span>)</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Rinsing the Nose</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Washing the Face</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Washing Both Hands to the Elbows</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Wiping the Head</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Wiping the Ears</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Wiping the Neck</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Wiping Both Feet</td></tr></tbody></table><h3>Obligatory Acts (<span class="inlineArabic">فرائض الوضو</span>) of <span class="inlineArabic">الوضوء</span>:</h3><table><thead><tr><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">1</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">2</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">3</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">4</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">5</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">6</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">7</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Pure Water</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Intention (<span class="inlineArabic">نیت</span>)</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Washing the Face</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Washing Both Hands (to the Elbows)</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Wiping the Head</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Washing Both Feet (to the Ankles)</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Order/Sequence (<span class="inlineArabic">ترتیب</span>)</td></tr></tbody></table><h3>Recommended Acts (<span class="inlineArabic">سنت الوضو</span>) of <span class="inlineArabic">الوضوء</span>:</h3><table><thead><tr><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">1</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">2</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">3</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">4</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">5</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">6</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">7</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">8</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">9</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">10</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">11</th><th style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">12</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Cleansing after Evacuation (<span class="inlineArabic">استنجا</span>)</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Washing Hands before putting them in the vessel</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Beginning with <span class="inlineArabic">بسم اللہ الرحمن الرحیم</span></td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Rinsing the Mouth (<span class="inlineArabic">کلی کرنا</span>)</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Rinsing the Nose</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Moving the Ring</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Combing the Beard with Fingers</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Wetting the Eyes</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Giving Preference to the Right Limbs</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Washing a Second and Third Time</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Wiping Both Ears</td><td style="text-align:center; vertical-align:middle;">Using the Miswaak (Tooth-stick)</td></tr></tbody></table><h2>Truth Concealment as Ingratitude</h2><p>There are many ways to conceal the truth, and sadly, many Muslims are in fact truth concealers. One can perform all the outward obligations of Islam and yet be concealing the truth from themselves. The very essence of truth concealment is ingratitude. A <span class="inlineArabic">کافر</span> is also known as an ingrate. Allah says:</p><p class="example">is ingratitude. A <span class="inlineArabic">کافر</span> is also known as an ingrate. Allah says:</p><p><br></p><p class="quote">is ingratitude. A <span class="inlineArabic">کافر</span> is also known as an ingrate. Allah says:</p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><div class="poetry-wrapper" data-content-type="poetry" data-id="0a20d749c5794c3fb0642f4cd617cd80" data-language="bilingual" data-poet="Rumi" data-type="poetry"><div class="poetry-section froala-poetry-container" data-original-text="والرب تعالى يقول: دَعَوا عَبدي، فأنا أعلمُ به، إذ أنشأتَهُ مِن الأرض Leave my slave alone. I know everything about him since the moment والرب تعالى يقول: دَعَوا عَبدي، فأنا أعلمُ به، إذ أنشأتَهُ مِن الأرض Leave my slave alone. I know everything about him since the moment"><div class="poetry-poet-header" style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center;"><h4 style="margin: 0; color: #722727; font-weight: bold; font-size: 1.2em;">Rumi</h4><button class="btn btn-sm btn-primary poetry-restore-btn froala-only-btn" title="Remove poetry formatting and restore plain text" type="button">&nbsp;Plain Text&nbsp;</button></div><div class="row"><div class="col-xs-12"><div class="poetry-couplet"><p class="h3 arabic-text text-center text-maroon" dir="rtl" style="margin-bottom: 5px;">والرب تعالى يقول: دَعَوا عَبدي، فأنا أعلمُ به، إذ أنشأتَهُ مِن الأرض</p><p class="text-center text-muted" dir="ltr" style="font-size: 2rem; margin: 0;">Leave my slave alone. I know everything about him since the moment</p></div><div class="poetry-couplet"><p class="h3 arabic-text text-center text-maroon" dir="rtl" style="margin-bottom: 5px;">والرب تعالى يقول: دَعَوا عَبدي، فأنا أعلمُ به، إذ أنشأتَهُ مِن الأرض</p><p class="text-center text-muted" dir="ltr" style="font-size: 2rem; margin: 0;">Leave my slave alone. I know everything about him since the moment</p></div></div></div></div></div><div class="ayah-card" id="ayah-card-14-34"><div class="golden-surah-header clickable-ayah-header" data-ayats="34" data-original-token="Q|14:34" data-surah="14" id="ayah-header-14-34"><span>Abraham (14:34)</span></div><p class="ayah-arabic">&rlm; &rlm;وَآتَىٰكُم مّن كُلّ مَا سَأَلْتُمُوهُ وَإن تَعُدُّوا۟ نعْمَتَ ٱللَّه لَا تُحْصُوهَا إنَّ ٱلْإنسَنَ لَظَلُومٌۭ كَفَّارٌۭ &lrm; <img class="ayah-number-img fr-fic fr-dii" src="https://myislam.sfo3.digitaloceanspaces.com/assets/2024/03/ayat/ayah-34.png" alt="34">&nbsp;&lrm;</p><div class="translation-header">Translation:.</div><p class="ayah-translation">And he gave you from all you asked of him. And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, mankind is [generally] most unjust and ungrateful.&nbsp;</p></div><p>Indeed man is extremely unjust and an ingrate. The word <span class="inlineArabic">كَفَّار</span> in this verse is not used in the meaning of &quot;disbeliever,&quot; but as &quot;ingrate.&quot; The sending of messengers is rooted in Allah&#39;s profound good intention toward His creation. If Allah had simply created humanity and withheld the manual for life, we would all be left to wander in a state of turmoil and darkness, clueless about our purpose.</p><p><br></p><div class="inserted-hadees ks-ahadees-container" data-collection="unknown" data-id="129" data-token="H|129" data-type="hadees" id="ahadees-1759610378590-646"><button class="delete-hadees-btn ks-ahadees-delete-btn" data-ahadees-id="ahadees-1759610378590-646" title="Delete this hadees">✕</button><div class="hadees-header ks-ahadees-header"><h4>Muhammad Ibn Abdullah (SWS)<span class="ks-ahadees-subject">- Accountability, Deeds</span></h4></div><div class="hadees-arabic ks-ahadees-arabic">حَاسِبُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ قَبْلَ أَنْ تُحَاسَبُوا، وَزِنُوا أَعْمَالَكُمْ قَبْلَ أَنْ تُوزَنُوا</div><div class="hadees-english ks-ahadees-english">Hold yourselves accountable before you are held accountable, and weigh your deeds before they are weighed</div></div><p><img src="Resources/IMAGES/212/8529ad6b-0a82-4c8e-bb53-2950453930b8.jpg" style="width: 425px;" class="fr-fic fr-dib imgResponsive fr-bordered" data-type="image" data-image-id="8529ad6b-0a82-4c8e-bb53-2950453930b8" data-session-id="212" data-insertion-id="17eaed9d-f5f8-4317-917d-30fbca59beea" data-content-type="image" alt="8529ad6b-0a82-4c8e-bb53-2950453930b8"></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><div class="esotericBlock"><div class="esoteric-header"><span class="esoteric-title">ESOTERICS</span></div><div class="esotericData"><p>This state of aimless wandering is reminiscent of the stories of Mulla Nasruddin. In one tale, Mulla Nasruddin is wandering the streets in the early morning hours. When a policeman asks him what he is doing, he replies, &quot;If I knew the answer to that, I&#39;d be at home in bed.&quot;</p></div></div><div class="etymology-container" data-content-type="etymology-basic" data-id="9bb7060625a542e5bca1293bec2def50" data-type="etymology-basic" style="width: 80%; margin: 40px auto; padding: 0 15px; box-sizing: border-box;"><div class="etymology-card"><div class="etymology-header"><h3 class="arabic-term">REFLECTION</h3></div><div class="etymology-details">This reflects the reality of many people who wander through life in a stupor, constantly seeking distractions and entertainment to avoid the pain of existence. The great scholar Rumi speaks of the many &quot;wines&quot; Allah has put on Earth to numb people&#39;s misery. He notes that Jesus (AS) was &quot;drunk in the love of Allah, while his donkey was high on barley.&quot;</div></div></div><p>&nbsp;</p><p><img src="Resources/IMAGES/212/db87d717-8f7f-482d-95ac-8ad5dc3b32e5.jpg" style="width: 435px;" class="fr-fic fr-dib imgResponsive fr-bordered" data-type="image" data-image-id="db87d717-8f7f-482d-95ac-8ad5dc3b32e5" data-session-id="212" data-insertion-id="d5d65529-534a-4a57-9177-2e3dff864c40" data-content-type="image" alt="db87d717-8f7f-482d-95ac-8ad5dc3b32e5"></p><p>This attitude of &quot;whatever gets you through the night,&quot; as John Lennon said, is a form of ingratitude from the Islamic perspective. The messengers have already brought the news and guidance, yet people refuse to accept it.&nbsp;</p><p><br></p><p>It is like being thirsty and given directions to a river, but choosing instead to watch a show or play a video game to forget the thirst. This is ingratitude.</p><p>Another story of Mulla Nasruddin illustrates a similar point: he was searching for his keys under a streetlight, and when someone asked him where he lost them, he pointed to a dark area away from the light. When asked why he was looking where he was, he replied, &quot;The light is better over here, right?&quot; This highlights another type of truth concealment: going where it is easy instead of where it is hard. This is where we begin to dilute religion to make our lives comfortable. Messengers, as human beings, set an incredible precedent by following Allah&#39;s Book to the letter, proving that what is decreed is humanly possible to achieve.</p><h2>Heedlessness and the Allegory of Plato&#39;s Cave</h2><p>The human condition is defined by heedlessness or forgetfulness, a state the Quran refers to as <span class="inlineArabic">غفلۃ</span>. We are distracted by the fleeting &quot;shine and glimmer&quot; of this world, lost in what can be likened to a &quot;vanity fair.&quot; A servant sent by the king to the marketplace gets sidetracked by a fair on the way. He gets lost in the fun, forgets his purpose, and by the time he realizes the sun has set, the marketplace is closed. This metaphor illustrates our immersion in heedlessness, where we become preoccupied with this world&#39;s powerful distractions.</p><p>So, how do we remind ourselves daily that this world is temporal and a greater journey awaits? From the Muslim perspective, the answer is remembrance, <span class="inlineArabic">الذکر</span>. This is why the Quran is also called <span class="inlineArabic">الذکر</span>&mdash;because it constantly reminds us of our true purpose. In contrast to our forgetful natures, messengers are awakened beings. All prophets share four common qualities:</p><ul><li>Truthfulness: they never lie.</li><li>Trustworthiness: their word is their bond.</li><li>Conveyance: they have the ability to articulate and convey the message.</li><li>Wakefulness: <span class="inlineArabic">فَطانا</span>.</li></ul><p>Messengers are individuals who have woken up to the truth, much like the freed prisoner in Plato&#39;s allegory of the cave. In Plato&#39;s story, prisoners chained since birth see only the shadows cast on a wall, mistaking these illusions for reality. When one prisoner is freed and dragged into the sunlight, he is initially disoriented and finds the truth hard to believe. But gradually, his eyes adjust until he can finally look at the sun itself&mdash;the ultimate source of light. He returns to the cave to share his discovery, but the other prisoners, comfortable in their ignorance, see his newfound &quot;blindness&quot; in the darkness as a sign of madness and violently resist his attempts to free them.</p><p>Plato presents this as an analogy for the challenges messengers face. The cave represents this <span class="inlineArabic">دنیا</span>, and the world outside the cave is the <span class="inlineArabic">آخرۃ</span>. Everything we see in this world is a mere reflection of the Hereafter. But people are often so comfortable in their ignorance that they become hostile to anyone who points out the truth. Worse, they aren&#39;t even interested in examining the proposition itself. This spiritual laziness is what is known as &quot;acedia.&quot; While often translated as sloth, in Christian theology, acedia was spiritual sloth&mdash;an unwillingness to seek the truth due to sheer arrogance.</p><p>Allah describes such individuals as <span class="inlineArabic">مُّقْمَحُونَ</span>. The term <span class="inlineArabic">مُقمَح</span> comes from camels: <span class="inlineArabic">قَمَحَ الجَمَل فَھُوَ قَامِحُون</span>. When a camel is brought to water, it may raise its head, refusing to drink. That is the essence of a <span class="inlineArabic">مقمح</span>. The messenger brings them to the river of knowledge to quench their thirst, but they are too arrogant to bow their heads and drink. They ask, &quot;The Quran? Why should I read that book?&quot; But one in every four people believes it is from Allah, which in itself is a good reason to be interested. It is because of this heedlessness that the Quran always juxtaposes <span class="inlineArabic">غفلۃ</span> (heedlessness) with <span class="inlineArabic">ذکر</span> (remembrance). As Allah says:</p><div class="ayah-card" id="ayah-card-30-7"><div class="golden-surah-header clickable-ayah-header" data-ayats="7" data-original-token="Q|30:7" data-surah="30" id="ayah-header-30-7"><span>The Romans (30:7).</span></div><p class="ayah-arabic">&rlm; &rlm;يَعْلَمُونَ ظَهرًۭا مّنَ ٱلْحَيَوٰة ٱلدُّنْيَا وَهُمْ عَن ٱلْآخرَة هُمْ غَفلُونَ &lrm; <img class="ayah-number-img fr-fic fr-dii" src="https://myislam.sfo3.digitaloceanspaces.com/assets/2024/03/ayat/ayah-7.png" alt="7">&nbsp;&lrm;</p><div class="translation-header">Translation:.</div><p class="ayah-translation">They know what is apparent of the worldly life, but they, of the Hereafter, are unaware.&nbsp;</p></div><p>The universal message of all prophets is <span class="inlineArabic">لا الہ الا اللہ</span>. The second part of the declaration of faith changes with each era, from <span class="inlineArabic">موسی رسول اللہ</span> to <span class="inlineArabic">عیسی رسول اللہ</span>, and finally, for us, <span class="inlineArabic">محمد الرسول اللہ</span>. All messengers were sent to remind humanity about Allah and pull them out of their state of heedlessness.</p><h2>The Debt of Submission: A Call from a Merciful Lord</h2><p>Our religion is called <span class="inlineArabic">دین الاسلام</span>. The word <span class="inlineArabic">اسلام</span> comes from the root <span class="inlineArabic">سلم</span>, meaning to submit, specifically, to willingly submit out of love for Allah. The word <span class="inlineArabic">دین</span> comes from <span class="inlineArabic">دَیْن</span>, which means debt. Therefore, our religion, <span class="inlineArabic">دینُ الاسلام</span>, literally translates to &quot;the debt of willing submission.&quot; The idea is that we have been endowed with innumerable blessings by our Lord, and for these blessings, we owe Him a debt of gratitude through our willing submission.</p><div class="ayah-card" id="ayah-card-3-83"><div class="golden-surah-header clickable-ayah-header" data-ayats="83" data-original-token="Q|3:83" data-surah="3" id="ayah-header-3-83"><span>The Family of Imran (3:83).</span></div><p class="ayah-arabic">&rlm; &rlm;أَفَغَيْرَ دين ٱللَّه يَبْغُونَ وَلَهُ أَسْلَمَ مَن فى ٱلسَّمَوَت وَٱلْأَرْض طَوْعًۭا وَكَرْهًۭا وَإلَيْه يُرْجَعُونَ &lrm; <img class="ayah-number-img fr-fic fr-dii" src="https://myislam.sfo3.digitaloceanspaces.com/assets/2024/03/ayat/ayah-83.png" alt="83">&nbsp;&lrm;</p><div class="translation-header">Translation:.</div><p class="ayah-translation">So is it other than the religion of Allah they desire, while to him have submitted [all] those within the heavens and earth, willingly or by compulsion, and to him they will be returned?&nbsp;</p></div><p>&nbsp;Allah questions whether we seek to avoid repaying this debt, when everything in existence is already doing so, willingly or unwillingly. The sun, a celestial body immense in size, rises and sets according to its decree, fulfilling its purpose. It is in a state of submission, yet the human being, insignificant in comparison, is not. The same applies to galaxies, mountains, rivers, and the animal kingdom; they all exist in a state of submission to their Creator. Even human beings must submit to their own nature&mdash;eating, drinking, sleeping&mdash;and to the limitations of their physical bodies. Everything in existence is paying back its debt of submission to its Creator, willingly or unwillingly&mdash;except the human being.</p><p>The crucial difference is that humanity is asked for willing submission (<span class="inlineArabic">طَوْعًۭا</span>), out of love, not by force (<span class="inlineArabic">كَرْهًۭا</span>). We will be held accountable for this debt on the Day of Judgment, <span class="inlineArabic">یوم الدین</span>, the day when this debt of willing submission falls due. It is also called <span class="inlineArabic">یوم الحساب</span>, the Day of Accountability. Rasul Allah (SWS) said in a Hadith:</p><div class="inserted-hadees ks-ahadees-container" data-collection="unknown" data-id="129" data-token="H|129" data-type="hadees" id="ahadees-1757669933719-742"><button class="delete-hadees-btn ks-ahadees-delete-btn" data-ahadees-id="ahadees-1757669933719-742" title="Delete this hadees">✕</button><div class="hadees-header ks-ahadees-header"><h4>Muhammad Ibn Abdullah (SWS)<span class="ks-ahadees-subject">- Accountability, Deeds</span></h4></div><div class="hadees-arabic ks-ahadees-arabic">حَاسِبُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ قَبْلَ أَنْ تُحَاسَبُوا، وَزِنُوا أَعْمَالَكُمْ قَبْلَ أَنْ تُوزَنُوا</div><div class="hadees-english ks-ahadees-english">Hold yourselves accountable before you are held accountable, and weigh your deeds before they are weighed</div></div><p>Interestingly, while we owe a debt to Allah, Allah also has a &quot;debt&quot; to us. When a master gives a command to a slave, the fulfillment of that command incurs a debt on the slave. If the slave obeys, the master owes him a reward. If he disobeys, he owes him a punishment. This is the essence of <span class="inlineArabic">یوم الدین</span>, the day when the debt falls due for both. This is why Allah says in the Quran:</p><p>Allah is asking for a loan, so that He can multiply its rewards and pay it back to His slave many times over. The ultimate reward for this beautiful loan is described as:</p><div class="ayah-card" id="ayah-card-57-11"><div class="golden-surah-header clickable-ayah-header" data-ayats="11" data-original-token="Q|57:11" data-surah="57" id="ayah-header-57-11"><span>Iron (57:11)</span></div><p class="ayah-arabic">&rlm; &rlm;مَّن ذَا ٱلَّذى يُقْرضُ ٱللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًۭا فَيُضَعفَهُ لَهُ وَلَهُ أَجْرٌۭ كَريمٌۭ &lrm; <img class="ayah-number-img fr-fic fr-dii" src="https://myislam.sfo3.digitaloceanspaces.com/assets/2024/03/ayat/ayah-11.png" alt="11">&nbsp;&lrm;</p><div class="translation-header">Translation:.</div><p class="ayah-translation">Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan so he will multiply it for him and he will have a noble reward?&nbsp;</p></div><p>This wake-up call is the very purpose of the messengers: to rouse humanity from its state of <span class="inlineArabic">غفلۃ</span>. The word <span class="inlineArabic">غفلۃ</span> is particularly interesting. In Arabic linguistics, words beginning with the letter <span class="inlineArabic">غین</span> often imply a covering, hiding, or veiling, such as <span class="inlineArabic">غاب</span> (to be absent) or <span class="inlineArabic">غفر</span> (to forgive). Our intellects, in a state of <span class="inlineArabic">غفلۃ</span>, become veiled by the temptations of this <span class="inlineArabic">دنیا</span>. A simpleton is called a <span class="inlineArabic">مُغَفَّل</span> because they are easily deceived. The term <span class="inlineArabic">غفلۃ</span> also means lactose intolerance, an inability to digest the most beneficial thing for mankind, which serves as powerful imagery for a person&#39;s refusal to accept divine benefit. Scholars have said that all sin and wrongdoing are rooted in <span class="inlineArabic">غفلۃ</span>, for if Allah was truly present in your heart, it would be impossible to sin. Allah asks in the Quran:</p><div class="ayah-card" id="ayah-card-82-6"><div class="golden-surah-header clickable-ayah-header" data-ayats="6" data-original-token="Q|82:6" data-surah="82" id="ayah-header-82-6"><span>The Cleaving (82:6).</span></div><p class="ayah-arabic">&rlm; &rlm;يَأَيُّهَا ٱلْإنسَنُ مَا غَرَّكَ برَبّكَ ٱلْكَريم &lrm; <img class="ayah-number-img fr-fic fr-dii" src="https://myislam.sfo3.digitaloceanspaces.com/assets/2024/03/ayat/ayah-6.png" alt="6">&nbsp;&lrm;</p><div class="translation-header">Translation:.</div><p class="ayah-translation">O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your lord, the generous.</p></div><p>As one scholar noted, Allah has put the answer to the question within the question itself. It is Allah&#39;s immense generosity, <span class="inlineArabic">کرم</span>, that has made us delusional. We are heedless about our sins because He does not react with immediate punishment. The people who are most loving and generous with us are often the ones we take for granted the most. Allah&#39;s immense mercy makes us bold in our transgressions because we forget that He is our Master, and that is <span class="inlineArabic">غفلۃ</span>.</p><p>An incredible Hadith describes a conversation between Allah and His angels, the oceans, and the earth. They say:&nbsp;</p><p>Not a single day passes that the oceans do not ask their Lord for permission to drown the children of Adam; and the earth asks its Lord for permission to swallow them; and the angels ask His permission to hasten their destruction and annihilate them. The earth says, &quot;O Allah, grant me permission to swallow them all. They walk on Your earth, eat from it, and do not prostrate to You!&quot; The angels exclaim, &quot;O Allah, grant us permission! In an instant we will annihilate this lot for their arrogance.&quot; The earth, oceans, and angels are Allah&#39;s creation, and they are filled with anger at seeing their beloved Creator disobeyed. But our Creator, the One we constantly ignore, says:</p><p><br></p>
